title: The effect of changing constituents on tensile mechanical properties of HfNbTaTiZr high entropy alloy: A molecular dynamics study.

recollection.starting_material: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy modeled with a random bcc solid solution
recollection.intervention: Atomistic molecular-dynamics simulations in which one or two elements were systematically removed or their concentrations varied, followed by uniaxial tensile loading at room temperature
recollection.structure: Single-phase bcc solid solutions with varying lattice distortion depending on which constituent elements were present
recollection.mechanism: Changes in local lattice distortion and atomic-size mismatch altered dislocation nucleation and motion; alloys retaining the largest size-mismatch elements (Hf, Zr) showed greater resistance to dislocation glide and thus higher strength
recollection.results: Guessed values: equiatomic alloy ~2.5 GPa yield strength and ~3.5 GPa ultimate tensile strength at 300 K. Removing Ta or Nb lowered strength by ~10–15 %, whereas removing the largest atoms (Hf or Zr) reduced strength by ~25 % and ductility by ~30 %. Young’s modulus ranged 120–140 GPa depending on composition.

score.note: The recollection broadly identifies composition variation via MD tensile testing and invokes BCC lattice distortion/dislocation mobility, but it misses the actual one-element-at-a-time 0–30 at.% substitution scheme. Its mechanistic trend is partly wrong: low Nb or Ta produced the strongest solid-solution strengthening, rather than strength being governed primarily by retaining Hf/Zr. Most numerical values and composition-dependent trends are inaccurate; only the modulus range is broadly plausible.
